name_reason: Follows data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=resource, descriptor=portrait_cache_id_list_base). Reflects the data type (a parallel list/array) and its role as a base pointer indexed with explicit *4 byte arithmetic (the code accesses it as [EDX + 0x53b17]). No Ghidra address residue: name carries no hex suffix matching its own address 0x53b17 or any data address; '40' is not embedded. Consistent with sibling globals data_fd2_resource_portrait_cache_count (@0x53BDF) and data_fd2_resource_portrait_cache_buffer_used (@0x539EC).
purpose: Parallel array of cached portrait IDs for the portrait sprite cache: id_list[k] holds the portrait_id resident in cache slot k.
logic_summary: Zero-init BSS, filled at runtime by fd2_load_portrait_to_cache. On first-time load it writes id_list[0]=portrait_id (MOV [0x53b17],ESI @0x1109d). On subsequent loads it scans id_list[0..count-1] for a cache hit (CMP ESI,[EDX+0x53b17], EDX=k*4 @0x11129) and, on a miss, appends id_list[count]=portrait_id (MOV [EDX+0x53b17],ESI, EDX=count*4 @0x11138). All access is full dword (uint32) with a 4-byte stride; ESI carries portrait_id. The list is parallel to the cache's sprite slots and valid for indices [0 .. portrait_cache_count-1].
datatype: uint32[40] (semantic; 40 four-byte portrait-id entries = 160 bytes). Ghidra applies byte[160] and the rebuilt src declares uint8[160]; both are 160 bytes and the code indexes with explicit *4 arithmetic. Type intentionally NOT changed this stage.
element_semantics: Each 4-byte (uint32) element = the portrait_id of the k-th cached portrait slot, parallel to the sprite-cache slots. Structural capacity is 40 entries because the cache frame-offset lookup table (0x780 bytes) holds 40 portraits x 12 sprites x 4 bytes.
notes: src comment block (src/rsrc/rsrc.c lines 773-794) is already precise and accurate: parallel-array semantics, 4-byte-stride dword access with writer/reader site addresses, 40-portrait capacity = 160 bytes rationale, and Ghidra-type note; matches disassembly exactly (WRITE @0x1109d, READ @0x11129, append @0x11138). Kept as-is. Ghidra plate already exists, is consistent with src (it even cross-references the rebuilt src declaration) and reaches the correct 160-byte conclusion; its 'Ghidra byte[40] undersizes' phrase is historical auto-type rationale (live Ghidra type is now byte[160], matching src), not a current contradiction, so plate left unchanged. is_const=false: game-side write-xrefs exist (stores at 0x1109d and 0x11138), so it is runtime-mutable zero-init BSS, not read-only (Ghidra .object2 block w=false attribute is not the deciding factor). No logic/equivalence issues found.
